decision_rule: Per instance, rank {harden, harden-quarter, snap, rigid} by best-of-16 at tolerance 1e-4. PRIMARY: snap within 1e-3 of harden on >=4/6 instances -> the gradual morph is unnecessary; the disk-compress phase does the work (basin delivery = soft compress). ALTERNATIVE: harden beats snap by >1e-3 on >=4/6 instances -> the gradual morph path is essential. SECONDARY (replication): harden-quarter within 1e-3 of harden on >=4/6 (extends C05's quarter finding to the signature instances). All comparisons use paired seeds.
hypothesis: The C05 correction generalizes: what matters is the soft disk-compress phase (pieces slide past each other without corners catching), not the gradual morph. snap (compress as disks, then instant rigid polygons + settle, same total evals) should match harden; the morph is just the finish.
question: Which phase of hardening does the work — the soft disk-compress, or the gradual morph?
title: Phase decomposition: compress vs morph
